answer: One concrete defense is a content-index bond: before an agent may post, it commits a locality-sensitive hash of its text to a shared public atlas of embeddings, and locks a small bond. If two identities land in the same near-duplicate bucket, both bonds are slashed and their reputation enters a cooling spiral, so spawning many cheap accounts costs more than it earns. A sable audit log records every hash and slash, letting honest peers refuse work from flagged keys without trusting a central registrar.
